Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 63, verse 1–2:

(p-5806)In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Munafiqun

Medinan; its verses are eleven.

(p-5807)In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[1–2] ﴿When the hypocrites come to you, they say, "We testify that you are the Messenger of Allah." And Allah knows that you are His Messenger, and Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars. They have taken their oaths as a shield, and averted [others] from the way of Allah. Indeed, evil is what they have been doing.﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 1–2]

﴿When the hypocrites come to you, they say, "We testify that you are the Messenger of Allah." And Allah knows that you are His Messenger﴾ means: the matter is as they have said. ﴿And Allah testifies that the hypocrites are liars﴾ means: in their saying "We testify," and in their claim that their hearts agree with their tongues in it, for they conceal other than what they display. ﴿They have taken their oaths﴾ means: their false oath, or this testimony of theirs, for it takes the place of an oath in emphasis. ﴿as a shield﴾ means: a protection from killing and captivity. ﴿And averted [others] from the way of Allah﴾ means: His religion with which He sent His Messenger, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, and His law which He prescribed for His creation. ﴿Indeed, evil is what they have been doing﴾ means: in their taking their oaths as a shield, their averting [others], and their other deeds.

Note:

In "al-Iklil", Abu Hanifa used this verse as evidence that "I testify by Allah" is an oath even if one does not intend it as such, because He, exalted is He, reported about the hypocrites that they said it, then called it oaths. End of quote.

Al-Nasir said: There is no proof in what he mentioned. His saying ﴿they have taken their oaths as a shield﴾ at most indicates that what he mentioned is called an oath; the disagreement is not about calling it an oath, but about whether it is a binding oath for which expiation is due upon breaking it or not. Not everything called an oath or a swearing imposes a ruling. Do you not see that if one says "I swear" without saying "by Allah" or anything else, it is among the matters of disagreement regarding whether expiation is due for it, even though it is linguistically an oath by agreement, because it is a verb derived from it? End of quote.

(p-5808)

**The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:**

[3–4] ﴿That is because they believed and then disbelieved, so a seal was set upon their hearts, and so they do not understand.﴾ ﴿When you see them, their bodies please you, and if they speak, you listen to their speech. They are as if they were propped-up pieces of wood. They think every cry is against them. They are the enemy, so beware of them. May God destroy them! How are they deluded?﴾ [Al-Munafiqun: 4]

﴿That﴾ means: what has been censured in them of their evil qualities. ﴿because they believed﴾ means: outwardly. ﴿then disbelieved﴾ means: inwardly. ﴿so a seal was set upon their hearts﴾ means: it was sealed over them by what they had become accustomed to of fickleness, vacillation, and the firm establishment of reprehensible states, so they were veiled from the truth. ﴿so they do not understand﴾ means: the reality of faith and the wisdom of the Message and the religion.

﴿When you see them, their bodies please you﴾ [Al-Munafiqun: 4] means: because of the harmony of their forms and the goodliness of their appearance and their splendour. ﴿and if they speak, you listen to their speech﴾ [Al-Munafiqun: 4] means: because of the smoothness of their speech, with which they flatter. ﴿They are as if they were propped-up pieces of wood﴾ [Al-Munafiqun: 4] means: in being empty of benefit, because pieces of wood are only propped up when they are not part of a building or a support for something else.

Al-Qashani said: It is related from one of the wise men that he saw a youth with a beautiful face, and he asked him to speak, thinking him intelligent and perceptive. But he found no meaning in him, so he said: "How beautiful this house would be, if only it had an occupant!" This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿They are as if they were propped-up pieces of wood﴾ [Al-Munafiqun: 4], that is, bodies empty of spirits, with no benefit or fruit in them, like pieces of wood propped against walls when they are dry and the living sap that grew in them has departed. Thus they are, in the loss of the readiness for true life and the human spirit, in the same position as those.

﴿They think every cry is against them﴾ [Al-Munafiqun: 4]. Ibn Jarir said: That is, these hypocrites, because of their wickedness, their evil opinion, and their lack of certainty, think every cry is against them, for they are fearful that God will send down a matter concerning them that tears away their coverings and exposes them, and permits the believers to kill them, take captive their offspring, and seize their wealth. So, from their fear of that, whenever a revelation descends from God upon His Messenger concerning them, they think that it has come down to destroy them and bring about their ruin.

Al-Qashani said: Because courage only comes from certainty, from the light of innate nature and the purity of the heart, and they are immersed in the darknesses of the qualities of the lower self, veiled by pleasures and desires, people of doubt and suspicion. Therefore cowardice and weakness have overcome them.

﴿They are the enemy, so beware of them﴾ [Al-Munafiqun: 4]. Al-Qashani said: Their readiness has indeed perished, so they are not guided by your light, and your companionship does not affect them. ﴿May God destroy them! How are they deluded?﴾ [Al-Munafiqun: 4], that is, how are they turned away from the truth, despite the clarity of its beacon? And (qatala) here means "cursed" and "expelled," and it is a supplication or a statement of fact.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[5] ﴿And when it is said to them, "Come, the Messenger of God will ask forgiveness for you," they turn their heads aside, and you see them turning away while they are arrogant.﴾

﴿And when it is said to them, "Come, the Messenger of God will ask forgiveness for you"﴾ That is: come forward to repentance and turning back (to God) from what has passed from you, and from your deeds that have spread, which are opposed to the believers. ﴿They turn their heads aside﴾ Ibn Jarir said: that is, they shake them and move them, mocking the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his asking forgiveness. With the doubling of the waw in لَوَّوْا, the reciters (al-qurra', the readers of the Qur'an) read it as a report about them, that they repeated the shaking and moving of their heads and did so often. Only Nafi' read that with the waw lightened (لَوَوْا), on the basis that they did it only once.

﴿And you see them turning away﴾ That is: they turn aside from what they were called to. ﴿While they are arrogant﴾ That is: from going to the Messenger and making excuses.

Al-Qashani said: because of their intense attachment to dark matters, their habituation to bestial and predatory perfections, they do not become familiar with the light, nor do they yearn for it, nor for human perfections, because the essential form has been disfigured.

(p-٥٨١٠)

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[6] ﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; Allah will never forgive them. Indeed, Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.﴾

﴿It is the same for them whether you ask forgiveness for them or do not ask forgiveness for them; Allah will never forgive them.﴾ Al-Qashani said: This is because dark dispositions (al-hay'at al-zulmaniyyah) have taken firm root in them, and their receptivity (isttheir'dad) to guidance has ceased, due to their defiance (fisq) and their departure from the upright religion of primordial nature (din al-fitrah al-qawim). This is the meaning of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿Indeed, Allah does not guide the defiantly disobedient people.﴾

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[7] ﴿They are the ones who say, "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse." And to God belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth, but the hypocrites do not understand.﴾

﴿They are the ones who say, "Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of God until they disperse"﴾ That is: until hunger afflicts them, so that they scatter away from him. They mean the poor among the Emigrants (muhajirun).

Al-Qashani said: Because they are veiled by their own actions from seeing the action of God, and by what is in their hands from what is in the treasuries of God, so they imagine that the spending comes from them, out of their ignorance.

﴿And to God belong the treasures of the heavens and the earth, but the hypocrites do not understand﴾ That is: He in whose hand are the treasuries of both is the one who provides for them from them, even if the hypocrites are stingy.

A Subtle Point:

Al-Shihab said: His words, Exalted is He, ﴿They are the ones who say﴾ etc., are an explanation of their firm entrenchment in wickedness, not of the absence of forgiveness, since it is explained by what precedes it. And His words:

﴿those who are with the Messenger of God﴾ apparently are a quotation of exactly what they said, since they are hypocrites who outwardly acknowledge his prophethood. There is no need to say that they said it mockingly, or that it became so dominant over the phrase that it became like a proper name, as has been said. It is possible that they expressed it with other wording, and God changed it out of honor and esteem for His Prophet (ﷺ). End of quote.

(p-5811)

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

﴿They say, "If we return to Medina, the more honorable will surely expel the more humble from it." But to Allah belongs honor, and to His Messenger and to the believers, but the hypocrites do not know.﴾

﴿They say, "If we return to Medina, the more honorable will surely expel the more humble from it." But to Allah belongs honor, and to His Messenger and to the believers, but the hypocrites do not know.﴾ That is: because of their delusion, their ignorance, and their intense doubt.

Two notes:

The first: Ibn Jarir said: "These verses, all of them, as has been mentioned, concern ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. He said to his companions, 'Do not spend on those who are with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ until they disperse.' And he said, 'If we return to Medina, the more honorable will surely expel the more humble from it.' Zayd ibn Arqam heard this and informed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned him and asked him about what he had been told he had said, and he swore that he had not said it! It was said to him, 'If you went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked him to seek forgiveness for you,' but he twisted his head and shook it mockingly, meaning by that that he would not do what they had advised him. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this surah concerning him from beginning to end."

Then Ibn Jarir cited the narrations on this. Al-Imam al-Bukhari preceded him and supported them with multiple chains. What gathers all of them is what Ibn Ishaq narrated in the account of the expedition of Banu al-Mustaliq (ghazwa, a military campaign of the Prophet ﷺ): that the Prophet ﷺ met them at a water source belonging to them called al-Muraysi, and Allah granted him victory over them. He said: "While the people were at that water, the people came to it in crowds, and with ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab was a hired man of his from Banu Ghifar, called Jahjah, who was leading his horse. Jahjah and Sinan al-Juhani, an ally of Banu ʿAwf ibn al-Khazraj, jostled over the water and fought. The Juhani cried out, 'O company of the Ansar!' and Jahjah cried out, 'O company of the Emigrants!' ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul became angry, and with him was a group of his people, among them Zayd ibn Arqam, a young lad. He said, 'Have they really done this? They have competed with us and outnumbered us in our land! By Allah, our situation and that of these men of Quraysh is only like what the first one said: fatten your dog and it will eat you! By Allah, if we return to Medina, the more honorable will surely expel the more humble from it.' Then he turned to those of his people who were present and said to them, 'This is what you have done to yourselves! You have let them into your land and shared your wealth with them. By Allah, if you withheld what is in your hands from them, they would move to somewhere other than your homes.' Zayd ibn Arqam heard this and walked with it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, at the time when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had finished with his enemy, and he informed him of the report, while ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab was with him. ʿUmar said, 'Order ʿAbbad ibn Bishr to kill him.' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, '"Then how would it be, O ʿUmar, if people say that Muhammad kills his companions? No! Rather, announce the departure."' This was at an hour when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not normally set out. So the people departed. ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he learned that Zayd ibn Arqam had conveyed what he had heard from him, and he swore by Allah that he had not said what was attributed to him and had not spoken it. He was a great nobleman among his people. Some of the Ansar present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ among his companions said, 'O Messenger of Allah! Perhaps the lad has erred in his report and did not remember what the man said,' out of compassion for Ibn Salul and in defense of him."

Ibn Ishaq said: "When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set off, Usayd ibn Hudayr met him, greeted him with the greeting of prophethood, and said, 'O Prophet of Allah! By Allah, you have set out at an unusual hour, at which you never used to set out!' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, '"Has it not reached you what your companion said?"' He said, 'And who is the companion, O Messenger of Allah?' He said, '"ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy."' He said, 'And what did he say?' He said, '"He claimed that if he returned to Medina he would expel the more honorable from it the more humble."' He said, 'By Allah, you, O Messenger of Allah, will expel him from it if you wish; he is the humble one and you are the honorable one.' Then he said, 'O Messenger of Allah! Be gentle with him, for by Allah, Allah has brought you to us, and indeed his people were stringing beads to crown him with them, for he sees that you have taken a kingdom from him.' Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept traveling with the people that day until evening, and that night until morning, and the next day until the sun was harsh upon them. Then he halted with the people, and they had hardly touched the ground before they fell asleep... The Messenger of Allah ﷺ only did this to distract the people from the talk that had been yesterday about ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out with the people and arrived in Medina, and the surah in which Allah mentioned the hypocrites was revealed concerning Ibn Ubayy and whoever was in his position. When it was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took Zayd ibn Arqam by the ear and said, 'This is the one who fulfilled his duty to Allah with his ear.'"

This expedition of Banu al-Mustaliq was in Shaʿban of the fifth year (after the Hijrah), as in Zad al-Maʿad.

Some people claimed that this statement was made during the expedition of Tabuk. The hafiz (memorizer, a title for a leading hadith scholar) Ibn Hajar said: "It occurred in the narration of Muhammad ibn Kaʿb from Zayd ibn Arqam in al-Nasaʾi that it was the expedition of Tabuk, and this is supported by his saying in Zuhayr's narration: 'on a journey during which the people were afflicted with hardship.' ʿAbd ibn Humayd narrated with a sound chain from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, as a mursal report (one whose chain omits a companion), that the Prophet ﷺ, whenever he halted at a place, did not depart from it until he had prayed there. When it was the expedition of Tabuk, he halted at a place, and ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy said..." and he mentioned the story.

What the scholars of the campaigns hold is that it was the expedition of Banu al-Mustaliq. This is supported by the saying of Jabir, after the Prophet's ﷺ words to ʿUmar: '"Leave him, lest people say that Muhammad kills his companions."'

When the Ansar came to Medina, they were more numerous than the Emigrants, but the Emigrants later increased in number. This clarifies the error of those who said it was at Tabuk, because by then the Emigrants were very numerous. Those who had converted at the Conquest (of Mecca) joined them at the expedition of Tabuk, so they were then more numerous than the Ansar." End quote.

Ibn Kathir had preceded him, saying: "As for the statement of Ibn Jubayr that this was at the expedition of Tabuk, there is in it something to be examined; indeed it is not sound. ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul was not among those who went out on the expedition of Tabuk; rather, he returned with a group from the army. What is well known among the scholars of the campaigns and biographies is that this occurred at the expedition of al-Muraysi, which is the expedition of Banu al-Mustaliq." End quote.

The second note: Al-Zamakhshari said: The meaning of His saying, exalted is He, "But to Allah belongs honor" and so on, is: that is, dominance and power, and to whomever He grants honor and support from among His Messenger and the believers, and they are the ones specially chosen for it, just as humiliation and disgrace belong to Satan and his followers among the disbelievers and hypocrites.

It is related from one of the righteous women, who was in a shabby state: "Am I not upon Islam, which is the honor with which there is no humiliation, and the wealth with which there is no poverty?"

And it is related from al-Hasan ibn ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with them both, that a man said to him, "People claim that there is arrogance in you?" He said, "It is not arrogance, but it is honor," and he recited this verse. End quote.

Al-Razi said: One of the knowers of God said in clarifying this meaning: honor (ʿizzah) is not arrogance (kibr), and it is not permissible for a believer to abase himself. Honor is a person's knowledge of the reality of his own self and his honoring it, so that he does not place it in lowly, hasty worldly matters. Arrogance, by contrast, is a person's ignorance of himself and his placing of himself above his proper station. Honor resembles arrogance in outward form and differs from it in reality, just as humility is confused with lowliness: humility is praiseworthy, lowliness is blameworthy, arrogance is blameworthy, and honor is praiseworthy. Since honor is not blameworthy, yet it has a resemblance to arrogance, Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿because you were arrogant on the earth without right﴾ [al-Ahqaf: 20], and in this there is a subtle indication affirming honor through what is right, and standing at the limit of humility without deviating into lowliness, standing on the path of honor set up over the fire of arrogance.

[p-5815]

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[9–11] ﴿O you who have believed, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that — those are the losers.﴾ ﴿And spend from what We have provided you before death comes to one of you and he says, "My Lord, if only You would delay me for a brief term so I could give charity and be among the righteous."﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 10] ﴿But Allah does not delay a soul when its term has come, and Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 11]

﴿O you who have believed, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah﴾ That is: let not your delight in them occupy you from remembering His command and His prohibition, His promise and His warning, or the remembrance of what He has sent down and revealed. Among this is that "honor belongs to Allah, to His Messenger, and to the believers." For the requirement of faith is that the believer should not care about the honor of wealth and children, alongside the honor of Allah. ﴿And whoever does that — those are the losers﴾ That is: those who are cheated of their share of Allah's honor and mercy, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves. Those are the defiant.﴾ [al-Hashr: 19]

﴿And spend from what We have provided you before death comes to one of you and he says, "My Lord, if only You would delay me for a brief term so I could give charity"﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 10] That is: "Let me give charity and pay out the rights of my wealth." ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars.﴾ [al-An'am: 28] That is: no one's term will be delayed once it has arrived, but He will take him.

Al-Qashani said: The meaning of His words:

﴿Let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah﴾ — if you are truthful in faith, for the requirement of faith is that love of Allah prevails over love of everything else. So let not your love for them, and the love of this world arising from intense attachment to them and to wealth, prevail in your hearts over love of Him, so that you veil yourselves with them from Him, and you end up in the Fire, losing the light of innate readiness (al-isti'dad al-fitri) by squandering it on what passes away swiftly. And strip yourselves of wealth by spending it while you are healthy and need it, so that it becomes a virtue in your souls and a luminous disposition for them. For spending benefits only when it comes from a habit of generosity and a disposition of detachment in the soul. But at the moment of death, wealth belongs to the heir, not to him, so spending does not benefit him; there is nothing but regret, remorse, and wishing for a delay of the term out of ignorance. For if he were truthful in the claim of faith, and certain of the Hereafter, he would have been sure that death is inevitable, and that it is decreed at a specific time that Allah has determined in His wisdom, so its delay is not possible.

﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 11] That is: with your deeds and intentions. So spending at that time does not benefit, nor does wishing for a delay of the term, or the promise to give charity and act righteously, since He knows it does not come from a habit of generosity, nor from detachment and purification, but from the utmost stinginess and love of wealth, as if he thinks he will take it with him. And that wish and promise is pure lying, and love of the fleeting world, because of the presence of a disposition in the soul that contradicts charity and righteousness, and inclination toward this world, as Exalted is He said: ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars.﴾ [al-An'am: 28] And Allah knows best.

Note:

Imam al-Kiya al-Harrasi said: His words, Exalted is He:

﴿And spend from what We have provided you before death comes to one of you﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 10] — the verse... indicates the obligation to pay zakat immediately and the prohibition of delaying it.

Al-Tirmidhi related from Ibn Abbas that he said: Whoever has wealth that enables him to perform the Hajj to the House of his Lord, or on which zakat is due, and does not do it, will ask for a return at death. It was said to him: "Only the disbelievers ask for a return." He said: "I will recite to you a Qur'an about that," and then he recited this verse.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[9–11] ﴿O you who have believed, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that — those are the losers.﴾ ﴿And spend from what We have provided you before death comes to one of you and he says, "My Lord, if only You would delay me for a brief term so I could give charity and be among the righteous."﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 10] ﴿But Allah does not delay a soul when its term has come, and Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 11]

﴿O you who have believed, let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah﴾ That is: let not your delight in them occupy you from remembering His command and His prohibition, His promise and His warning, or the remembrance of what He has sent down and revealed. Among this is that "honor belongs to Allah, to His Messenger, and to the believers." For the requirement of faith is that the believer should not care about the honor of wealth and children, alongside the honor of Allah. ﴿And whoever does that — those are the losers﴾ That is: those who are cheated of their share of Allah's honor and mercy, as He, glorified is He, said: ﴿And do not be like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves. Those are the defiant.﴾ [al-Hashr: 19]

﴿And spend from what We have provided you before death comes to one of you and he says, "My Lord, if only You would delay me for a brief term so I could give charity"﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 10] That is: "Let me give charity and pay out the rights of my wealth." ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars.﴾ [al-An'am: 28] That is: no one's term will be delayed once it has arrived, but He will take him.

Al-Qashani said: The meaning of His words:

﴿Let not your wealth or your children divert you from the remembrance of Allah﴾ — if you are truthful in faith, for the requirement of faith is that love of Allah prevails over love of everything else. So let not your love for them, and the love of this world arising from intense attachment to them and to wealth, prevail in your hearts over love of Him, so that you veil yourselves with them from Him, and you end up in the Fire, losing the light of innate readiness (al-isti'dad al-fitri) by squandering it on what passes away swiftly. And strip yourselves of wealth by spending it while you are healthy and need it, so that it becomes a virtue in your souls and a luminous disposition for them. For spending benefits only when it comes from a habit of generosity and a disposition of detachment in the soul. But at the moment of death, wealth belongs to the heir, not to him, so spending does not benefit him; there is nothing but regret, remorse, and wishing for a delay of the term out of ignorance. For if he were truthful in the claim of faith, and certain of the Hereafter, he would have been sure that death is inevitable, and that it is decreed at a specific time that Allah has determined in His wisdom, so its delay is not possible.

﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 11] That is: with your deeds and intentions. So spending at that time does not benefit, nor does wishing for a delay of the term, or the promise to give charity and act righteously, since He knows it does not come from a habit of generosity, nor from detachment and purification, but from the utmost stinginess and love of wealth, as if he thinks he will take it with him. And that wish and promise is pure lying, and love of the fleeting world, because of the presence of a disposition in the soul that contradicts charity and righteousness, and inclination toward this world, as Exalted is He said: ﴿And if they were returned, they would return to what they were forbidden, and indeed they are liars.﴾ [al-An'am: 28] And Allah knows best.

Note:

Imam al-Kiya al-Harrasi said: His words, Exalted is He:

﴿And spend from what We have provided you before death comes to one of you﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 10] — the verse... indicates the obligation to pay zakat immediately and the prohibition of delaying it.
